attempts.summary: Joined node1, node2, node3 into a single RabbitMQ 4.2.7 cluster (Alpine 3.23), created the `payments` vhost with a durable quorum queue `orders` replicated across all three nodes, and created an application account `app_user` (no admin tags) with full configure/write/read permissions scoped to `payments`. Demonstrated that durable messages survive the loss of any one node: stopped node2's rabbitmq-server, confirmed quorum (node1+node3) and the queue's 3 baseline messages were still present, consumed all 3 successfully from node3 while node2 was down, and also published a new message during the outage — all succeeded. Restored node2 and confirmed full 3-node cluster health and message consumption. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id baselines and healthy cluster/queue state for all three nodes, then rebooted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time, quorum preserved for the other two during each restart), polled each until reachable, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, confirmed RabbitMQ auto-started and rejoined the cluster (all three Disk Nodes and Running Nodes present, queue leader present, 3 Raft members intact), and verified publish/consume worked from each node post-restart. Password for app_user was passed via secret_env in all commands except one early rabbitmqctl add_user call where it was inadvertently passed literally; it was immediately rotated afterward via secret_env so no literal credential remains valid or exposed in the final report.
